U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services

Non-Precedent Decision of the Administrative Appeals Office

In Re: 28773401

Date: MAY 27, 2025

Appeal of Nebraska Service Center Decision

Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker (Extraordinary Ability)

The Petitioner, a professional violinist, seeks classification as an individual of
extraordinary ability in the arts. See Immigration and Nationality Act (the Act) section
203(b)(1)(A), 8 U.S.C. § 1153(b)(1)(A).

The Director of the Nebraska Service Center denied the petition, concluding that the record
did not establish that the Petitioner meets at least three of the ten initial evidentiary
criteria at 8 C.F.R. § 204.5(h)(3)(i)-(x). The matter is now before us on appeal. Upon de
novo review, we will sustain the appeal.

I. ANALYSIS

The Petitioner claims to have satisfied four criteria, relating to lesser nationally or
internationally recognized prizes or awards, published material about the Petitioner,
display of the Petitioner's work at artistic exhibitions or showcases, and leading or
critical role for distinguished organizations.

Documentation of the beneficiary's receipt of lesser nationally or internationally recognized
prizes or awards for excellence in the field of endeavor. 8 C.F.R. § 204.5(h)(3)(i).

The Petitioner received first prize at two international violin competitions. The record,
including media coverage of the competitions and evidence of their selective character,
establishes that these are nationally and internationally recognized prizes for excellence
in the field. The Petitioner meets this criterion.

Published material about the beneficiary in professional or major trade publications or other
major media, relating to the beneficiary's work in the field. 8 C.F.R. § 204.5(h)(3)(iii).

The record contains reviews and profiles of the Petitioner published in major media,
including national newspapers of record. The Petitioner meets this criterion.

Evidence of the display of the beneficiary's work in the field at artistic exhibitions or
showcases. 8 C.F.R. § 204.5(h)(3)(vii).

The Petitioner has performed as a featured soloist at internationally recognized venues and
festivals. We agree with the Petitioner that this evidence satisfies this criterion.

Evidence that the beneficiary has performed in a leading or critical role for organizations or
establishments that have a distinguished reputation. 8 C.F.R. § 204.5(h)(3)(viii).

The Petitioner serves as concertmaster of a nationally prominent orchestra. The record
establishes both the distinguished reputation of the organization and the leading nature of
the concertmaster role. The Petitioner meets this criterion.

II. FINAL MERITS DETERMINATION

Because the Petitioner has satisfied the initial evidentiary requirement, we turn to a final
merits determination, considering the totality of the record. The evidence, viewed in the
aggregate, demonstrates that the Petitioner has sustained national and international acclaim
and that she is among the small percentage at the very top of her field. The record further
establishes that the Petitioner seeks to continue work in her area of extraordinary ability
and that her entry will substantially benefit prospectively the United States.

III. CONCLUSION

The Petitioner has established eligibility for the classification sought.

ORDER: The appeal is sustained.
